title: LLM isolation X8 follow-up: the triage floor sets still come from prose, and the triage decision has no attempt binding
summary: Review of #1131. At isolation.i8.stage=enforce, triagecap refuses a triage-decision.json without committed_floors, but deferred_floors stays optional, and the evalgate floor binding (go/internal/evalgate/floorbinding.go) still reads DeferredFloorPackagesDecl and CommittedFloorPackages with the report prose as the fallback. triagecap.Recorder counts prose floors when the triage-cap stage is below enforce. The host projection (triagedecision.Derive/Project) writes no committed_floors, so a projected decision fails the clamp at enforce. A triage-decision.json from an earlier triage dispatch of the same cycle survives (deliverable.HostEffects.derive skips an existing file), so it has no attempt binding. NewPlanJudge and NewBridgeRetryAdjudicator have no production caller; wire them with their Signal Center option or delete them. Spec: docs/architecture/llm-isolation.md §12.1.
fix: At enforce: make deferred_floors required in the triage schema, make the evalgate floor binding and Recorder refuse the prose fallback, have the projection write committed_floors from the report only when the agent declared them, and clear or attempt-bind triage-decision.json at each triage dispatch. Decide the two unwired seats.
acceptance: At enforce no floor set in evalgate or Recorder comes from report prose; a test for each
A stale triage-decision.json from an earlier dispatch cannot decide the clamp; a test that fails with the fix reverted
NewPlanJudge and NewBridgeRetryAdjudicator have a production caller with signals, or are removed with their tests
